newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bank executives welcome rating upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bank executives welcome rating upgrade.

text.p: Argentine bank executives said Thursday the upgrade to the country's credit rating by Standard & Poor's will lower borrowing costs, attract more investment and improve confidence.

"This could imply larger investments in the markets, easier access to international credit for Argentine firms and more confidence in the economy in general," Ruben Beraja, president of the Association of Argentine Public and Private Banks, told Reuters. S&P raised Argentina's long-term foreign currency debt rating to BB from BB-.

"This is a very favorable decision for the Argentine economy and it will raise the readiness of investors to invest," Norberto Peruzzotti, the executive director of the Association of Argentine Banks, said in an interview.

Both executives said the news is a sign of rising confidence in the economy. Peruzzotti said the upgrade was "especially thanks to the government's efforts in maintaining the fiscal deficit within prudent limits."
Beraja did not rule out another upgrade in the future, but he added that it will be "fundamental to reach the fiscal targets. Not only to reach them, but to reduce public expenditure."
